title: Relative ampleness for schemes survives arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ and $g:T'\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and put $X'=X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to T'$. Suppose that for every affine open $V\subseteq T$, $L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then for every affine open $V'\subseteq T'$, $(g'^*L)|_{(f')^{-1}(V')}$ is ample, where pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 0893 (lemma-ample-base-change), with relative ampleness as in Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample). The affine-open hypothesis already implies quasi-compactness of f.

An f ample line bundle remains relatively ample after any morphism to the base scheme
